lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Lourdes, it's Rachel. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not bad. Sleeping better.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, yes. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've picked your days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You feel like you have to do something.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the overnight fast fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the overnight fast going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stop eating at 8, I just need tea at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to finish eating by 7 on 5 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 7. Maybe 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to finish eating by 7 on 5 nights. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Lourdes, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Suggests finishing dinner by 7; neutral framing.
Offers three days; commitment to try.
Adds meaning: openness plus need for fit.
Pushes 5 days after participant said 3; pressure.
Fear of recurrence; family support as reasons.
Identifies a plan that makes it doable.
Notes growing recognition of small changes.
Doubts the value of the fast.
Moves past doubt to scheduling; sustain talk not explored.
Invites participant to set the plan.
Reflects momentum and desire to continue.
Proposes own cutoff time; tea allowed.
Explores imagined benefits of sustaining change.
Sets specific goal: finish eating by 7, five nights.

flags.reason: Pushes a 5-day target after participant offered 3; no permission or collaboration.
Sustain talk 'I don't really see the point' was not explored; coach moved to scheduling.
Overnight fasting advised for a diabetic patient without asking about medications or hypoglycemia risk.

score.summary: Rachel used many good reflections and open questions, and Lourdes built a specific goal of finishing eating by 7 on five nights with a confidence rating of 7 to 8. The coach pushed the frequency from three days to five, did not explore the 'I don't see the point' doubt, and did not check fasting safety for a diabetic patient or set a next contact.
strengths: Line 8: asked permission before offering the dinner suggestion.
Line 49: 'Why a 7 and not a 4?' drew out her reasons and family motivation.
Line 51: clear summary of the plan with a check for accuracy.
coaching_tips: Line 20: after she said three days, ask permission or invite her to choose the number rather than pushing five.
Line 29: explore 'I don't really see the point' with a reflection or open question before moving to scheduling.
Line 10: before advising an overnight fast with diabetes, ask about her medications and hypoglycemia symptoms or suggest checking with her care team.
Close by setting a next contact and reviewing how the prior week's goal went.
